articles.title: ‘Damage control’ after EC row: Congress demands SIR rollback, CEC’s resignation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Congress on Saturday demanded the immediate suspension of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and called for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Congress on Saturday demanded the immediate suspension of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and called for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation or prosecution. Their demand comes after the Election Commission issued a fresh statement defending its decisions amid reported differences within the poll body.Congress leaders Pawan Khera and Jairam Ramesh accused the EC of going into "damage control" mode following an Indian Express report and subsequent media coverage on differences between the three election commissioners. The party alleged that the SIR exercise had led to the "disenfranchisement" of crores of voters and questioned the Commission's explanation on changes to Form 6, used to add names to electoral rolls."The ECI's press note today is too lame, too little, too late," Congress' head of media and publicity department Pawan Khera said.Ramesh said the Commission had issued the statement only after the media reports and nationwide protests seeking Kumar's removal."It has just issued a wishy-washy Press Note that raises further questions on its intent, integrity, impartiality and credibility," he said on X."The ongoing SIR, which has turned out to be a method of massive disenfranchisement of several crores of Indians, must be suspended immediately without delay."In the meantime, nothing short of the CEC's resignation or prosecution will suffice," he said in a two-page statement.Congress questions EC's explanationThe Election Commission said all SIR orders were issued after approval from all three Election Commissioners. It also said changes to Form 6 had been upheld by the Supreme Court.The Commission further said letters written by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary were not related to any policy decision of the Commission or its IT division. According to the EC, the letters concerned the functioning of an officer deputed to the poll body.Ramesh said the EC statement did not directly deny the findings reported by the Indian Express."First, the Press note does not directly deny the story or its findings. It makes a defensive attempt to downplay the same in paragraph 3(i) and 3(ii) but does not say that the allegations are baseless," he said.On Goa, he said the EC's response showed that 81 of the 97 deleted voters had already filled Form 6 to be included again in the electoral rolls."To put this another way, you disenfranchise voters through a broken and corrupt system, and when caught say that they are being added back," Ramesh said.Khera also alleged that the EC had not addressed objections raised by the other two Election Commissioners over changes to Form 6."That objection was not resolved then. It was not resolved since. And this 'mother of all objections' has still not been addressed - even after today's so-called unanimous meeting," Khera said on X."So until the ECI answers this specific legal objection, no length of press notes, no claim of unanimity or any other clownery can save Gyanesh Kumar Gupta's face," he said."It is still not too late for him. He should resign and turn approver, or prepare for jail," Khera added.Congress raises questions over voter deletionsRamesh also questioned the EC's reliance on a Supreme Court order of May 27 saying the order had preceded the recent media revelations."The order which was pronounced well before the recent revelations will not save the CEC for the malicious deletion of targeted voters, for the incompetence that has resulted in citizens being wiped off the roles, for the crores lost in both expenses and man-hours due to the confusion and harassment caused to entire families," he said.He also questioned the extension of voter registration deadlines in Delhi and Maharashtra and asked what would happen to voters in Karnataka, Telangana, Bihar and West Bengal."What happens to the voters disenfranchised in Bihar and West Bengal? Do the voters of these and other states who were deleted due to one man's corruption not deserve answers," Ramesh said.The Congress leader also criticised the EC's decision to involve experts from IITs and IIITs to review the ECINET portal and submit a report on whether it complies with rules."Aside from being a meaningless safeguard (since the concern is not about the technical soundness but rather the centralization which prevents voter addition at ground level) this confirms the concerns attributed to the two other Election Commissioners per the reportage," he said.Dispute over Gen Z votersRamesh alleged that the EC's statement had not addressed concerns over the deletion of young voters."The Press Note avoids answering the questions regarding the deliberate targeting of Gen Z voters. The ECI has no answer for its targeted disenfranchisement, beginning mid-July through wholly illegal changes made to Form 6 (unseen and unapproved by Parliament) which placed an unfair burden on them to find and disclose their parents and/or grandparents' details," he said.He listed several allegations that he said required answers, including the "unilateral nature of decision making by the CEC", alleged bias against the Opposition, alleged participation in "vote chori", the enrolment of Gen Z voters and alleged negligence in the deletion and updating of electoral rolls.Ramesh said the CEC could not avoid scrutiny through bureaucratic procedures."He stands exposed and is now petrified as an entire country seeks to hold him accountable," Ramesh said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: South African police discover body of 10th woman near Johannesburg
articles.summary: Police are investigating the killings in a country with one of the highest femicide rates in the world.
articles.body:
South African police have discovered the body of another woman east of the country’s commercial capital, Johannesburg, bringing the total number of female bodies found near the city since mid-July to 10.

Police confirmed the discovery in Thembisa, Ekurhuleni, on Saturday but have not provided any further information. The body was found in the morning, according to the daily newspaper, The Sowetan.

The discovery adds to growing concern over violence against women in a country long plagued by violent crime. While police work to establish whether the killings are connected, there have been community concerns that the murders are being carried out by the same killer or killers.

Provincial police chief Tommy Mthombeni said the latest victim appeared to have been stoned to death, and a post-mortem examination would be conducted to determine the cause of death.

“We have put highly capable investigators on this case,” he told reporters at the scene, pledging to find those responsible for the killings.

President Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged the latest discovery while on the campaign trail for upcoming local elections, broadcaster eNCA reported.

“I’ve sadly heard about 10th body of a woman found in Thembisa,” Ramaphosa said. “This continues to make us very sad, and in many ways, it’s a shame on the men of South Africa that we continue to kill the women of our beautiful country.”

South Africa has one of the highest femicide rates in the world, with an average of 15 women killed per day.

Two women have been charged with the murder of the woman whose body was the ninth discovered, last week. Police have said that the killing may have stemmed from a relationship-related matter.

Mthombeni told state broadcaster SABC that investigators believe the ninth killing was an isolated case. However, he said it is possible some of the other killings are connected.

He added that some of the murders shared similarities, but cautioned that there is no conclusive evidence to suggest the same person or group is responsible.

Police discovered three bodies in July and August within six kilometres (four miles) of one another in Ekurhuleni. Earlier this month, six bodies were found in 10 days, also in Ekurhuleni.

Prior to Saturday’s discovery, all of the deceased women were in their 20s or 30s. Several of them were found completely or partially nude. Police have not yet confirmed the age of the 10th woman or whether she was clothed.

The first body, discovered in mid-July, was found naked. The deceased had been restrained with cable ties. Her boyfriend was subsequently arrested, but no charges were filed.

articles.body: SRINAGAR: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk walked back his comparison between Ladakh and Tibet, saying he meant only to highlight the gravity of the violence in Leh on Sept 24 last year and had no intention of hurting Tibetans. The Leh Apex Body member apologised Saturday after the Central Tibetan Administration in Dharamshala objected to his remarks as “misplaced and inaccurate”.“I was only comparing a specific incident on a particular day and of course not with decades of sufferings that Tibetan people have gone through,” Wangchuk said. “I have no intentions whatsoever to cause any hurt to anyone, least my dear Tibetan friends... I deeply apologise from the core of my heart,” he said in a Facebook post.CTA spokesperson Tenzin Lekshay said Friday that comparing Ladakh with Tibet was inaccurate. “Tibet continues to remain under China’s authoritarian rule,” he said, adding that Tibetans face systematic repression of fundamental rights and religious freedom, along with measures aimed at erasing their distinct cultural identity.Wangchuk made the comparison Thursday while addressing people in Leh on the first anniversary of Sept 24 police firing on protesters demanding Sixth Schedule status and statehood. Four people were killed and nearly 90 injured after demonstrations turned violent.He said he feared an “encounter” for speaking out against what he called atrocities in Ladakh. “Today, such atrocities are being committed in Ladakh that even China is not doing in Tibet,” he had said.On Saturday, the activist said he understood the suffering of Tibetans and had “always opposed Chinese repression”, but contended that those who witnessed Sept 24 violence in Leh might understand his comparison.Wangchuk said in the town of about 20,000 people, four were killed and one died by suicide, while 75 were arrested and faced charges, including attempt to murder. articles.title: Groundswell of support sees Bury St Edmunds' venue reopen
articles.summary: The family behind a music arts centre says its revival has been boosted by local support.
articles.body:
A groundswell of local support has led to a music venue reopening, its owner has said.

There were fears in March that the Hunter Club in Bury St Edmunds, Suffolk, could close down after its long-time manager left .

However, there was an outcry from musicians and after almost four months, the grassroots music centre reopened in August - and it has been hosting a weekend of live performances to mark its comeback.

Lucy Allen, a member of the Hunter family who own the club, said: "The local music community stepped up and said, 'this is really important and we want to help you get the club back on its feet'."

Allen, the centre's joint manager, added that locals wanted to "turn it back into something which is really needed in Bury St Edmunds".

"We've been working with lots of wonderful people, and it's a really strong grassroots music space and we're also trying to do that for the arts as well, so... visual arts theatre, language, dance."

The venue, in St Andrew's Street South, has provided a platform for bands and performers to showcase their music since 2009.

The centre underwent months of refurbishment, and its reopening has been welcomed by a string of local musicians who have been taking to its various stages at this weekend's Roomsfest event.

Josh Read, 24, from Suffolk band Decoupage, said: "Venues like this, and the rehearsal space connected to it, are vital as it's how bands get started and they eventually progress to playing bigger places.

"These promoters give them a chance while they're still cutting their teeth and learning their craft - without places like this there would be no live music.

"The prospect of this place was soul crushing... it's a lifeline for young bands starting up."

Fellow musician Sybbie Hoggar, 18, from thrash metal outfit Hello Kitty Funland, said: "It's important that we have places to go that aren't school or home.

"People value community a lot and it's really important that there's a space for that to happen."

Witnesses spotted Bradley walking in his apartment complex with a container, and when he realized he was seen, he dropped the container and ran into his apartment, Smyrna Police Lt. Meredith Holt said during a news conference Friday. Witnesses called the police after finding human remains inside the container, Holt said. GEORGIA PAIR CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER BARTENDER'S DISMEMBERED REMAINS FOUND IN LAKE OUTSIDE ATLANTA Police had previously responded to his home after a missing woman’s family reported her car and phone were at the location, Holt said, but they did not execute a search warrant. After the witnesses found the human remains, police returned with a search warrant for Bradley’s car and found a garbage bag pulled tightly, "showing the outline of a body part," according to a news release from the department. SINGER D4VD PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO MURDER OF YOUNG GIRL ALLEGEDLY FOUND DISMEMBERED, DECOMPOSING IN HIS CAR Police called the Cobb County Medical Examiner’s office, which confirmed the bags contained human remains. I’ve been in law enforcement for 25 years and I have been a part of multiple homicide cases and I’ve worked crimes against children for 16 years, and this is a particularly gruesome crime," Holt said during the news conference. articles.title: A Pennsylvania grandfather built a backyard amusement park with a 105-foot waterslide, go-kart track and vintage carousel; his $24,700 roller coaster then triggered a zoning fight
articles.summary: Michael Chorba, a 60-year-old grandfather in Pennsylvania, has spent years turning his backyard into a private amusement area for his family.
articles.body: Michael Chorba, a 60-year-old grandfather in Pennsylvania, has spent years turning his backyard into a private amusement area for his family. The property already has a go-kart track, a 105-foot waterslide and a vintage carousel. But his latest project, a small roller coaster, has led to a zoning dispute with local authorities.Chorba’s roller coaster, called The Tidal Wave, was built as part of his hobby of restoring vintage amusement rides for his grandchildren. According to Centre Daily Times, the coaster has a footprint of about 34 by 72 feet, while its tallest part, the control station, is about 18 feet high. Chorba said he spent about $20,500 on the coaster itself, another $2,500 on new vinyl decals and $1,700 on lighting.The project is now at the centre of a dispute in Mount Pleasant Township because local zoning rules do not specifically allow such a structure. Chorba said the situation is unusual for the small township. “It’s a small township. They’ve never dealt with anything like this before,” he said as quoted by Centre Daily Times.The dispute comes after years of Chorba building and restoring attractions on his property. He said he had worked on the go-kart track for 25 years with the help of friends and family before taking a long break from such projects. His return to the hobby began with a waterslide, which he bought in 2021.How Chorba built the backyard attractionThe waterslide was not a complete commercial ride. Chorba bought a portion of a large slide that had been used at a ski resort and then built the supports himself. He also gave it a theme based on Jurassic World, adding dinosaurs around the attraction.Mount Pleasant Township zoning officer Ed Sanders said the waterslide does not face the same zoning problem. According to Sanders, water slides are covered under the township’s municipal planning code, meaning its size and where the slide originally came from do not affect whether it is allowed.Chorba later added another major attraction to the property. He bought a 1957 carousel made by the Allan Herschell Company for $28,000. After buying it, he and his team repainted the horses and carriages, replaced the leather stirrups and reins, and had an electrician wire the structure.Chorba then applied for a zoning permit to build a large gazebo on his property. Once the gazebo was built, he moved the carousel inside it. The carousel, waterslide and go-kart track were therefore already part of the property before the roller coaster became the focus of the zoning dispute.Why the roller coaster was rejectedSanders said the local law prohibits structures that are not explicitly permitted. Because the municipal code does not specifically mention roller coasters, the township had to consider whether the attraction could legally remain on the property.“Not too many municipalities will include a roller coaster or amusement park rides, especially not in rural Pennsylvania. Something out of the ordinary would have to happen,” Sanders said.Sanders noticed the roller coaster last spring and advised Chorba to apply for a zoning permit. As expected, the permit was rejected, after which Chorba was advised to seek a variance.The variance request was then considered by the township's zoning board. One of the board's three members had to recuse himself because he is a close neighbour of Chorba, Sanders said. That left two members to decide the request.One member moved to approve the roller coaster, but the other did not second the motion. Without the required second, the request could not move forward. “It had to be denied because it couldn’t be approved,” Sanders said.Chorba says it is a family playgroundFor Chorba, the roller coaster is not meant to become a public amusement park. He said the attraction is intended only for his family and grandchildren.“You’re really creating wholesome fun for the kids, instead of keeping them stuck inside on electronics all day,” Chorba said.The coaster is still being restored. Chorba and his family were waiting for new lap bars to complete the project. He said removing the ride would be particularly difficult for his youngest granddaughter, who lives with him. “She would be really devastated, because she considers it part of her play area,” Chorba said.He also said some people had suggested that he turn the property into a petting zoo or another type of attraction to get around the zoning rules. But Chobra rejected that idea, saying he does not want to operate a public attraction. “I just want to do this and keep it as our family’s little playground,” he said.After the zoning board did not approve the variance, Chorba appealed to the county court. The court sent the matter back to the zoning board. Sanders said another hearing will likely take place once the official decision is returned to the board.You use AI every day. articles.body: Pune: Farmers and activists in Solapur have urged the administration to immediately conduct crop inspections and prepare panchanamas following govt’s declaration of drought in 11 tehsils on Saturday.The identified tehsils are North Solapur, South Solapur, Barshi, Akkalkot, Mohol, Madha, Karmala, Pandharpur, Sangola, Malshiras and Mangalwedha.With crops nearing the final stage of cultivation, farmers fear delays could affect assessment of losses and access to relief measures.Activist Sandeep Kumbhar said officials should begin the exercise without delay and complete it on a “war footing”.“The growth of sugar cane fields across the district is stunted and the overall harvest will be extremely low. articles.title: Tens of thousands attend right-wing protest over Ceuta migrant crisis
articles.summary: Demonstrators are demanding early elections and accuse Pedro Sanchez’s government of negligence.
articles.body:
Thousands of people have rallied in the Spanish capital to protest the government’s policy on irregular migration and its handling of a recent migrant influx into the North African enclave of Ceuta.

Saturday’s protest in Madrid was organised by right-wing civil society group Sociedad Civil Espanola and backed by the mainstream conservative People’s Party (PP) and far-right Vox.

According to the government, 20,000 people attended, while protest organisers put the turnout at 180,000.

At the end of July, more than 70,000 migrants stormed into the autonomous Spanish city of Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco, before most of them were returned. However, thousands remain stranded .

Demonstrators accused Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and his government of failing to protect the borders of Ceuta.

They are calling for an early election to be held by mid-November, with Vox demanding Sanchez be tried for treason. Spain’s next general election is not due until August 2027.

PP’s secretary-general Miguel Tellado said there was a “widespread feeling that the government has not acted responsibly; there has been a dereliction of duty, extreme negligence”.

“Spanish society has to take to the streets to ask the government to defend our territorial integrity,” he added.

The July 30 and 31 surge of people into Ceuta led to unprecedented scenes and the deaths of dozens of migrants.

Sanchez said on Tuesday that Moroccan border control failed to adequately handle the incident and that an investigation was still under way, adding that Rabat had been asked for answers.

The Spanish government estimates that between 6,000 and 10,000 stranded migrants remain in Ceuta.

Vox leader Santiago Abascal is demanding that everyone who arrived in late July be deported to their country of origin.

Abascal said Ceuta remained “invaded because Sanchez continues to be Morocco’s servant”.

Spanish newspaper El Pais reported on Saturday that the government is planning to approve a decree on Tuesday to accelerate the return of migrants from Ceuta to Morocco.

The protest is the second under the March for Dignity banner. That demonstration was held in late May before the incident in Ceuta and attracted 40,000 protesters, according to the government.

articles.title: Of Azad & another shade of blue in UP politics
articles.summary: Chandrashekhar Azad, Bhim Army founder and Azad Samaj Party chief, wins Nagina Lok Sabha seat; eyes UP polls and Delhi rally on Dalit reservation.
articles.body: Manjari MishraIt was a roadside sign welcoming visitors to Ghatrauli in Saharanpur district that catapulted the blink- and -miss hamlet onto the national spotlight over a decade ago. What exactly caught public eye was hard to tell — the unusual words “Great Chamar welcomes you to Ghadkauli”, or the young man standing beside the sign, donning dark aviators, bleached bright fitted shirt , with a natty royal blue scarf snaked around his shoulders, staring insolently into the camera. Spunky, smart alecky, saucy — Chandrashekhar Azad is all that and much more. Founder of Bhim Army, chief of the Azad Samaj Party and now MP from Nagina, the 39 -year-old has perfected the art of blending hard-edged Ambedkarite rhetoric with political theatre.Nothing about this master provocateur seems to be accidental -- especially the swaggering gait, the well-choreographed body language of an action hero or the punchy dialogue delivery cleverly designed to fuel adrenaline and project an image of a born rebel. As his ambitions sore beyond Nagina, the self-styled ‘Neela-Baaj’ (blue hawk) has his eyes trained on the upcoming electoral battlefield in UP. Also beyond it as far as Delhi where in its trademark brazen show of political machismo, the ASP chief proposes to hold a “massive public rally” on Dalit reservation.Azad’s political trajectory has been equally eventful. After experiencing caste discrimination as a student, he emerged as a local activist advocating for Dalit rights. In 2014, he and three associates co-founded the Bhim Army, a pressure group aimed at empowering marginalised communities through education and self-defence training. Initially, the organisation had a limited presence. Then came the billboard.Soon, the young activist from Saharanpur became a recognised face across western UP. The timing proved crucial. The BSP was reeling from its disastrous performance in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, its traditional support base appeared unsettled and the aura surrounding party supremo Mayawati seemed diminished. Sensing an opportunity, Azad intensified efforts to strengthen his grassroots presence and expand the Bhim Army’s reach beyond western UP.The defining moment came in 2017 during the Saharanpur caste violence involving Dalits and Thakurs. Azad and several associates were arrested on charges related to incitement and later jailed. His 16 months in prison, including the final months under the National Security Act, earned him significant attention and sympathy among sections of Dalit youth. Recognising the political potential of that support, he launched his own party.The date was carefully chosen: April 14, Ambedkar Jayanti. The symbolism was unmistakable. Azad sought to position himself as a new-generation claimant to the political legacy of B.R. Ambedkar and Kanshi Ram.Politics, however, proved more challenging than activism. In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the ASP fielded 111 candidates. Azad himself contested the Gorakhpur Urban seat, the political stronghold of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The result was decisive. He secured only 7,640 votes and suffered a heavy defeat.Undeterred, Azad returned to the political arena in 2024, contesting the Nagina parliamentary constituency as an independent candidate. This time, he confounded sceptics. In a constituency with a substantial Muslim population, a sizable Dalit base and significant OBC representation, Azad successfully stitched together a broad social coalition. The strategy worked. articles.title: Hamas slams Board of Peace for refusal to work with UNRWA in Gaza
articles.summary: Hamas accuses Board of Peace of aligning with Israel after excluding UN agency for Palestinians from Gaza operations.
articles.body:
Palestinian group Hamas has condemned the Board of Peace’s decision not to work with the United Nations agency for Palestinians, UNRWA, and for saying that the agency will have no role in Gaza.

The US-created Board’s decision is “a complete alignment with the Zionist [Israeli] position”, aimed at ending UNRWA’s operations, preventing it from delivering aid to Palestinians and eliminating the right of return, Hamas spokesperson Hazem Qassem said on Saturday.

On Friday, the Board of Peace said that “UNRWA’s involvement in Gaza is unchanged.”

“We will only work with trusted partners who will deliver for the people of Gaza and contribute to a deradicalized Strip,” it said in a post on X, adding that “UNRWA fails on those litmus tests”.

In his statement, Qassem said it was “strange for the Peace Council to adopt this hostile stance towards UNRWA while simultaneously failing to provide aid to Gaza or compel the occupation to abide by the ceasefire agreement and halt the daily killings of Palestinians in the Strip”.

UNRWA , set up in 1949, has for decades provided aid and education services to Palestinian refugees and preserved their national rights.

Palestinians see the agency as safeguarding their right of return to their homeland, while Israel wants it dismantled.

The Associated Press reported on Friday that Board of Peace members had been more willing to work with UNRWA behind the scenes than their public stance suggested.

At the Board of Peace briefing to the UN General Assembly on Wednesday, officials named several UN agencies as partners. UNRWA was not among them.

However, a Board of Peace official, speaking to The AP on condition of anonymity, confirmed that board members had met UNRWA officials several times.

The official said the agency’s programmes could continue if they served Gaza’s residents well, but maintained that “UNRWA’s days are over”.

Philippe Lazzarini, who led UNRWA until earlier this year, told The AP that members of the Palestinian technocratic committee appointed by the Board to govern Gaza wanted to work with the agency.

On Thursday, Lazzarini accused the Board of failing to deliver on its mandate, saying in a post on X that Israeli authorities are still blocking basic aid “as part of a wider plan to keep Gaza unlivable for Palestinians”.

“Grandiose plans is what the Board of Peace does best. Plans however will not keep the people of Gaza warm this winter,” he added, urging that crossings into Gaza be opened and supplies let in at scale.

On the ground on Saturday, Israel’s pattern of violations against Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank continued.

Israeli attacks killed seven Palestinians across the Gaza Strip in the past 48 hours, including one person who succumbed to wounds sustained prior, Gaza’s Ministry of Health said.

In northern Gaza, Israeli forces shot dead a Palestinian in Jabalia, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. An Israeli drone strike near Joulis Street and al-Nouri Tower in the Nuseirat refugee camp killed another person and wounded others.

In al-Mawasi in Khan Younis, an Israeli drone strike wounded several Palestinians, including a girl, while Israeli artillery shelled areas east of the city.

An Israeli quadcopter also opened fire on Salah al-Din Street in central Gaza, wounding three people, including another girl.

Meanwhile, in the occupied West Bank, Israeli forces stormed Ramallah-based Birzeit University, raiding one of its buildings while students sat final examinations, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa.

In Tulkarem, forces arrested resident Bashar Odeh after raiding his home in Shuweika, and interrogated others during home searches in Zeita.

In Bethlehem governorate, Israeli forces closed the military gates at the entrances to western villages, stopping residents, including pedestrians, from passing.

Raids continued across other localities, including the Qalandiya and Am’ari refugee camps.

articles.title: 80 aircraft, 40 countries, 1,500 personnel: IAF’s biggest air exercise Tarang Shakti kicks off in Jodhpur;  US, France envoys hail multinational drill
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Nearly 40 countries, 80 aircraft, including 30 foreign fighter jets and transport planes, 1,500 military personnel and one destination: Jodhpur
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Nearly 40 countries, 80 aircraft, including 30 foreign fighter jets and transport planes, 1,500 military personnel and one destination: Jodhpur air base. Indian Air Force’s second edition of the country’s biggest multinational air exercise Tarang Shakti took off in Rajasthan on Saturday with the airspace over the desert state set to witness over a thousand sorties by both Indian and foreign fighters over the next fortnight.Welcoming air force guests from around the world, IAF in a post on X on Saturday said, “A warm welcome to our friends from across the skies as they touch down at Jodhpur. Welcome to India. Welcome to Tarang Shakti.”Seven countries are participating directly with their advanced aircraft and fighter assets while 32 nations are attending as observers. The key aircraft attractions of Tarang Shakti, which will go on till Oct 12, are six US fifth-generation stealth fighter jets, F-35s, which for the first time are participating in the air exercise in India, seven French Rafales, UAE’s six F-16 jets, MRTTs, KC-135s and Australia’s C-130 aircraft, alongside IAF fighter jets like Sukhois, Tejas, Mirage-2000 and Indian Rafales.In a post on X on Saturday, US ambassador Sergio Gor said, “American airpower has arrived in Jodhpur! Six F-35 Lightning IIs and 200+ Airmen are now in India for their first-ever participation in Exercise Tarang Shakti. Excited to see America’s premier fifth-generation fighters make its Tarang Shakti debut, flying alongside the IAF MCC and partners.”The exercise will cover a wide spectrum of missions, including counter-air operations, air defence, close combat, airlift and air-to-air refuelling, along with more complex mission sets involving multiple aircraft and forces.Looking forward to France’s participation in Tarang Shakti, French ambassador Thierry Mathou said: “India is a core strategic defence partner of France. Regular participation in bilateral military exercises with India such as Varuna at sea, Garuda in the air and Shakti on land, as well as multinational exercises such as Tarang Shakti pave the way for greater Indo-French operational coordination and military interoperability. France’s involvement in this exercise illustrates our shared commitment to ensuring regional and global security and upholding international law and freedom of navigation in the Indo-Pacific region, in which France is a resident power.”

articles.title: New Form 6 enrolments where no SIR is under way won't need mapping
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Those applying for fresh enrolment as electors through Form 6 in locations other than the 12 states and UTs where special intensive revision
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Those applying for fresh enrolment as electors through Form 6 in locations other than the 12 states and UTs where special intensive revision (SIR) is currently underway will no longer need to attach a declaration mapping themselves or their relative to the electoral rolls from the last SIR.In the states and UTs where SIR is going on, Form 6 will continue to be accompanied by a mandatory declaration by the applicant listing their or their relatives' electoral rolls details from the last SIR, apart from their father's, mother's and spouse's names and their respective EPIC numbers, if available.A statement put out by the three-member Election Commission Saturday justified the continued requirement of new electors to submit the declaration along with Form 6 as part of SIR, saying "the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Supreme Court".For the non-SIR period, the forms applicable as per the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used, the commission added. The declaration was first added to Form 6 in the SIR order issued for Bihar on June 24, 2025.Sources told TOI the system will revert to the pre-SIR Form 6 with immediate effect in non-SIR states/UTs, including the states due for polls early next year.As exclusively reported by TOI on Sept 25, a special summary revision will be undertaken in these poll-bound states later this year.Both election commissioners, SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had in May and Aug, respectively, sent internal notes to the deputy election commissioner concerned, opining that Form 6 can only be amended by the govt.This was after they had approved of the declaration attached to the form as part of three SIR orders. While election commissioner Vivek Joshi raised objection to the revised Form 6 format on May 16 this year, Sandhu endorsed it on Aug 13, well after Supreme Court had upheld the SIR process. Their concerns were later echoed by opposition parties led by Congress, which alleged that Form 6 was changed "unilaterally" by CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The EC statement Saturday, however, put on record that all three SIR orders - issued on June 24, 2025, for Phase 1 Bihar; on Oct 27, 2025, for Phase 2 in 12 states; and on May 14, 2026, for the ongoing Phase 3 in 19 states/UTs - were unanimously approved by the CEC and the two commissioners. To eliminate any scope for doubt, EC added Saturday's statement was also issued with the "approval of the full commission".The declaration required to be attached to Form 6 itself has undergone a change since it was introduced in the SIR order for Bihar. The Bihar declaration required those seeking fresh enrolment to declare their or their parents' date and place of birth and submit proof of the same from the list of 11 documents attached to the SIR order, though this list was not exhaustive. This declaration was revised for subsequent phases of SIR, introducing mapping to the last SIR instead of seeking proof of citizenship.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: New-build homeowner finds 150 faults days after moving in
articles.summary: Getting the keys to a new home felt like a dream come true, until this couple found 150 faults.
articles.body:
It was the day Georgina and Charles Barnes had waited three years for - collecting the keys to their first home.

But when the brand new property was inspected just days later by a Welsh snagging company - the final quality check by independent inspectors - they identified 150 defects, including incorrectly installed fire barriers, signs of a previous leak and what they called "exceptionally poor" workmanship.

Swansea-based New Home Quality Control was set up by John Cooper after he became fed up of being asked to hide things from customers on building sites.

It is the responsibility of developers to make sure new-builds meet regulations, according to the National House Building Council (NHBC).

The couple are far from alone when it comes to issues with new houses.

Written evidence submitted by the New Homes Ombudsman Service said the Home Builders Federation national new homes customer satisfaction survey, published in March 2025, showed 93.7% of new-build buyers reporting defects or snags to their developer after moving in .

Just over a quarter of buyers also found more than 15 problems in their new-build home.

"We just wouldn't have known," said Georgina.

"If there had been a fire, that's one thing that could have happened and been very detrimental."

Georgina, 36, and her husband saved for three years to buy a house, before falling in love with the development in south Leicestershire.

As moving day approached, social media began serving her a steady stream of new-build horror stories

After paying £299,995 for the house, she said getting it snagged was "non-negotiable".

"It just felt unbelievable that we'd finally done it," she added.

"We actually finally got our own place. This is ours. This is ours to do what we want with. It just felt great."

But the report also identified improperly roofing defects, low water pressure and what inspectors described as "exceptionally poor" installation of the gas meter cabinet and gas pipe.

More than a dozen of additional cosmetic and finishing defects were also recorded throughout the property

As they had a two-year warranty from the developer, it meant they fixed the issues.

"I would say for any new-build buyer, 100% no doubt, I recommend a snagger," Georgina said.

Vistry, responsible for the housing developer Countryside, which built Charles and Georgina's house, said it supported "appropriately conducted independent inspections as an additional source of reassurance about build quality".

It said each home is checked by its teams and independent inspections take place and, two to three weeks after customers move in, the build team meets to discuss and agree any snagging work.

Such issues are not new to John Cooper, 50, co-founder of New Home Quality Control.

He said, while working as a contracts manager in 2018: "The site manager asked me to hide something from a customer that was moving in the next day."

This was the tip of the iceberg after he had seen poor quality workmanship over about six years.

"From that moment on, I thought to myself 'I've got to make a change in this industry somehow. This can't continue'," he said.

Cooper spoke to his supervisor at the time, Lee Challenger, 42, and the two men quit their jobs and started New Homes Quality Control.

"We've never inspected a house and found absolutely nothing wrong with it," he said.

The most common defects involve brickwork, carpentry and roofing, he said.

"It's always going to be carpentry issues and bricklaying issues.

"I just think that there's not enough quality bricklayers to build the amount of properties that the developers are building across the UK on a yearly basis."

The team also regularly identifies missing or incorrectly installed weep vents - which are installed in exterior walls to let moisture escape.

Cooper said some developments had even featured "fake" weep vents, where decorative plastic pieces had been fitted instead of functioning openings.

"They thought they could get away with it," he said.

Cooper said before new owners get the keys, the NHBC inspects the property and sign it off.

"I'm sick of hearing every property being signed off, because if that was the case, then we wouldn't have a company," he said.

Many of Cooper's clients get emotional when they see how many issues there are with their new houses.

"There were some quite serious issues in their new property and they had spent all their life savings on it."

Cooper said his long-term goal was for every new-build home to undergo an independent inspection before its owners moved in.

"If someone's spending their life savings on a house, they deserve to get what they paid for," he said.

The inspections take between two and four hours, depending on the size of the house, and cost about £349-£499.

Among the arsenal of tools the snaggers use are drones, GoPro cameras, cavity cameras, thermal imaging equipment and laser levels.

But not everyone can afford their services as they spend all their money on the house.

NHBC said it is the responsibility of the builders to ensure they meet building regulations and homeowners must raise any issues with the house builder within two years - if they are not fixed can seek resolution via NHBC.

The organisation said it carries out inspections at "key stages of the build" and "provide feedback" on the quality.

Home Builders Federation (HBF), which represents the building industry said: "New homes are not made in a factory.

"They are bespoke products, built by numerous tradespeople, often on sites exposed to all weathers, and it is inevitable that on occasions there are some snags."

It said the "vast majority of snagging issues are minor" and there was no evidence that quality standards were not keeping pace with the rate of housebuilding.

While there is a need for more homes, house-building levels are flatlining due to "major barriers" preventing their construction, it said.

But "quality and service levels remain extremely high" and there is "no evidence" that labour shortages are affecting the new homes.

"Although the industry does face skills challenges in some areas, as does the wider construction industry, we are currently building around 200,000 homes a year versus a need to deliver around 300,000 with no sign of output increasing," it said.

HBF said it would support statutory registration for builders with the New Homes Quality Board but warned that snagging inspectors were not regulated.

"Customers need to take care that any inspector they use is suitably qualified and accredited by a professional body, such as RICS," it added.

"We do not believe additional blanket inspections are necessary. There is already a comprehensive framework of regulation, building control, warranties and builder quality assurance in place."

Property developers Taylor Wimpey refused to comment, and Watkin Jones, Barratt Redrow and Persimmon Homes did not respond for comment.

The Welsh government said it was committed to making sure homebuyers get high quality and are protected if things go wrong.

The UK government said it was investing £39bn in affordable housing and pledged £625m to train up to 60,000 construction workers.

articles.title: Otra noche que se llenó de estrellas
articles.standfirst: Un año más y durante cinco horas, con todo tipo de actividades, participación ciudadana y la Plaza de España como sede central, Madrid se convirtió en un polideportivo gigante
articles.summary: Un año más y durante cinco horas, con todo tipo de actividades, participación ciudadana y la Plaza de España como sede central, Madrid se convirtió en un polideportivo gigante
articles.body: La última vez, Madrid aún no había recibido a los campeones del mundo con una rúa formidable. La última vez, Madrid aún no había dado el pistoletazo de salida para una temporada que desembocará en el Metropolitano, sede la final de la Champions. La última vez, Madrid aún no se había convertido en Madring para acoger en el nuevo circuito urbano para un Gran Premio de F1. La última vez, eso sí, Madrid ya respiraba deporte. Y la anterior. Y la anterior a la anterior... Esa última ya se ha convertido en la penúltima, después de que ayer tuviera lugar una nueva edición de la Noche del Deporte, la cuarta bajo el paraguas de MARCA y del Ayuntamiento de Madrid, que por otra parte sirvió para repetir escenario. La Plaza de España aspira a convertirse, por ubicación, por logística y por ambiente, en la sede definitiva de un evento ineludible, desarrollado esta vez de 20.00 a 01.00 horas, léase de la lenta caída del sol al emocionante arranque de la madrugada, léase también de sábado a domingo. La de España, pero no sólo la de España. También la de Oriente o la de Cibeles, contextos incomparables sin necesidad de un largo desplazamiento para repartirse danza urbana (ofrecida por The X Hod), esgrima, exhibiciones de gimnasia artística y gimnasia rítmica o, en el marco de las artes marciales, Nihon Tai Jitsu. En realidad La Noche del Deporte pertenece a toda una ciudad, apurando Comunidad, porque Madrid daba la bienvenida a todo aquél que quisiera acercarse. Y fueron muchos, a fe que sí. De Villanueva de la Cañada, a poco más de 30 kilómetros de la capital, es Lucía Martín-Portugués. No podía tener la velada mejor madrina que la flamante campeona de Europa de sable. Ni mejor padrino, por cierto, que Oriol Cardona, campeón olímpico de esquí de montaña (y bronce en el relevo mixto). Ambos tomaron el relevo de Fátima Diamé y Miguel Ángel Moya, que lo habían sido en 2025, y ambos se sometieron a los pertinentes retos propuestos en relación con sus respectivos deportes. Movistar apoyó la Noche con varias iniciativas, patrocinando por ejemplo el campo de fútbol de dimensiones reducidas, conocido como la 'jaula', en el que pudo desempeñarse todo el que se hubiera registrado al efecto, o la zona de pickleball, deporte de moda que combina elementos del bádminton, del tenis y del pádel y en el que algunos ofrecieron sus primeros golpes desde el apoyo de monitores especializados. El set Radio MARCA by Movistar permitió además a los aficionados seguir la previa, el desarrollo y el análisis posterior de ese Inglaterra-España que se jugaba en Wembley. CaixaBank volvió por su parte a impulsar una Noche accesible, apoyando el deporte para las personas con discapacidad. Una de las primeras actividades, de hecho, fue la exhibición de baloncesto en silla 3x3 entre CD Ilunion (equipo español más laureado) y Rehatrans Getafe BSR. El fútbol de ciegos también tuvo su momento, comprobando parte del personal lo complicado que es marcar un gol con antifaz puesto y el sonido de los cascabeles incorporados al balón como única referencia. El hyatlón no es deporte paralímpico pero permite que sea competitivo todo el que lo practique: por ejemplo, Kini Carrasco y Carmen González, protagonistas también de la jornada. Tenth y Byd completan la lista de patrocinadores para un evento que durante sus cinco horas también tuvo hueco y tiempo para las actividades dirigidas de Forus, el atletismo, el baloncesto (Fernando Romay desde su grandeza haciendo las delicias de los más pequeños), los dardos (con algunos de los grandes especialistas nacionales), los deportes mentales (del ajedrez al Go, pasando por el Scrabble), el golf (simulador última generación), el tenis de mesa, la zona Gaming (Gran Turismo como reclamo), el gimnasio en la calle que puso Brooklyn Fitboxing, el pentatlón moderno... En realidad la relación se alarga incluyendo actividades deportivas de nuevo cuño (floorball, flag football, roundnet, subsoccer, teqball...), apariciones como la de la mascota de Miami Dolphins o premios como el que recibió Inter JP FInancial con motivo de sus Bodas de Oro con el fútbol sala... De todo, oiga. Porque no merecía menos la ocasión. Otra Noche del Deporte para el recuerdo. Afortunados los que la vivieron, afortunados los que la seguirán viviendo. Habrá más, sólo faltaba. Y de Madrid al cielo, por supuesto.

articles.title: INDIA bloc to meet on Sept 30, CEC's ouster on top of agenda
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Opposition INDIA bloc will meet on Sept 30 to discuss the alleged manipulation of poll rolls under SIR and a possible joint struggle to press
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Opposition INDIA bloc will meet on Sept 30 to discuss the alleged manipulation of poll rolls under SIR and a possible joint struggle to press for the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The meeting has been scheduled against the backdrop of nationwide outrage triggered by revelations that ECs SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had questioned many of the decisions regarding SIR.The opposition, led by Rahul Gandhi, has said the revelations tie in with their allegations of 'vote chori' in favour of BJP over the last two years. It has demanded the scrapping of the SIR process.TMC MP Derek O'Brien said the demand for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation is "non-negotiable", while other issues will also be discussed at the meeting. "We will work unitedly and purposefully."The meeting is expected to be attended by the leading lights of the anti-BJP front, including Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Uddhav Thackeray and MA Baby.The meeting has been scheduled after CPM's MA Baby wrote to parties (including AAP, DMK and CJP) seeking an immediate meeting.Trinamool's Mamata Banerjee also reached out to INDIA bloc members. She called the CEC "Vanish Kumar", demanded his ouster and said the Bengal mandate was stolen.The joint brainstorming will follow a Congress Working Committee meet on Sept 29.The parties are also planning to submit a fresh "removal notice" against Kumar in both Houses of Parliament.CPI-ML's Dipankar Bhattacharya said that there is a strong belief within INDIA bloc that some parties (Aam Aadmi Party and DMK) which are not part of the alliance umbrella should also be roped in to boost the campaign. It also released a fact-finding report regarding SIR in constituencies that the party lost narrowly in recent Bihar assembly polls and claimed it found 17-25% of voters had been wrongly deleted.The meeting assumes special significance as Cockroach Janata Party and other youth outfits have already announced a stir over the issue.CJP has reiterated that it will launch a nationwide agitation from Mumbai on Oct 2 after its ultimatum seeking the resignation of Kumar ended Saturday. Azad Maidan is most likely to be the venue of its protest.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
